chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Dawood al-Raqqi, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made for acts of kindness (al-ma'ruf) a people from His creation, making them love its performance; and He directed the seekers of acts of kindness to seek them out, and made their fulfillment easy for them, just as He made the rain easy for the barren land, so that it may revive it and revive its people through it.

And indeed, Allah made for acts of kindness enemies from His creation, making the acts of kindness hateful to them and making their performance hateful to them; and He prohibited the seekers of acts of kindness from seeking them, and prohibited their fulfillment upon them, just as He withholds the rain from the barren land to destroy it and destroy its people.
And what Allah pardons/forgives is more abundant.

key_terms.لِلْمَعْرُوفِ: Acts of kindness / customary good deeds

ai.seo_question: How does Allah facilitate or hinder acts of kindness among different people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine distribution of capacity for *al-ma'ruf* (kindness/good deeds), contrasting those whom Allah has made beloved to the doers of good with those whom He has made hated by them. Using the metaphor of rain, he illustrates how this divine disposition either nurtures spiritual life or leads to destruction, emphasizing that despite these distinctions, Allah's forgiveness remains predominant. This hadith highlights the Shia concept of *tawfiq* (divine facilitation) as a gift that enables consistent righteous action.
